newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off but uptrend intact.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off but uptrend intact.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures came off highs not seen in over two months to end slightly easier on Thursday but dealers said the market remained on track to reach a target of 19,000 points in the near future.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract subsided from a peak of 18,965 to end at 18,655, 75 points below its previous close.
Market turnover was a low 12,560 lots and dealers said liquidity was likely to decline further ahead of Japan's Golden Week holidays.
"It was very technical trading today. The charts have turned bullish but when we got above 18,950, people started to sell it down," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
He said the June Nikkei could see more downside but was likely to hold above 18,500 and head towards the 19,000-19,200 area where more resistance was likely.
A senior trader with an Asian institution said Tokyo stocks also seemed to be benefiting from a possible switch of funds out of U.S. equities.
"We'll probably consolidate around 18,600-18,950 before we head higher. We should test 19,000 very soon," he added.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 358.0 against its opening 360.0 on volume of 1,641 lots.
